chapter_title: Improving a Resource with AI Agents
learning_objective: The learner will classify each of thirteen fixes under the rubric metric it mainly raises, with at least 11 of 13 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** fix-metric-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of thirteen fixes under the rubric metric it mainly raises, with at least 11 of 13 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** All thirteen fixes of the chapter section "The Fix Toolkit", and the ten metrics of Chapter 3 (all defined in this chapter above this block or in earlier chapters). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each fix the learner commits one of eight metrics. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct metric column in Content. Mastery is at least 11 of 13 correct on the first attempt. Reading the fix summary table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Every fix raises the accessibility metric. (2) One fix raises only one metric and never affects another. (3) Practice questions raise the readability metric. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying fixes by the metric they mainly raise is an Understand-level action that lets the learner choose a fix from a low score. Thirteen fixes spread over eight metrics teach the learner which fix belongs to which gap. **Content:** The eight metric bins: Accessibility, Readability, Accuracy and currency, Open license, Modularity, Metadata, Editable source, Practice with feedback. The thirteen fixes: | # | Fix | Correct metric | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | AI alt text generation | Accessibility | Alt text is a WCAG text alternative. | | 2 | Caption generation | Accessibility | Captions serve learners who cannot hear the video. | | 3 | Heading repair | Accessibility | A clean outline serves screen reader users. | | 4 | Reading level rewrite | Readability | It moves the text toward the audience's grade. | | 5 | Glossary generation | Readability | It defines terms the audience may not know. | | 6 | Link repair | Accuracy and currency | A working link is part of a current resource. | | 7 | Content update | Accuracy and currency | It replaces an outdated fact. | | 8 | Metadata generation | Metadata | It fills the record's descriptive fields. | | 9 | License statement repair | Open license | It completes the license and credit statements. | | 10 | Chapter splitting | Modularity | It makes modules that stand alone. | | 11 | PDF-to-Markdown conversion | Editable source | It turns a locked file into one that anyone can revise. | | 12 | Practice question generation | Practice with feedback | It adds questions with answers and explanations. | | 13 | MicroSim building | Practice with feedback | It adds an interactive activity with feedback. | **Provenance:** The pairs follow the chapter section "The Fix Toolkit" and the metric definitions of Chapters 4 through 10. The sim notes that a fix can affect more than one metric and that each pair shows the main metric. **Rules:** Each fix has exactly one correct metric. Accessibility holds three fixes. Readability, Accuracy and currency, and Practice with feedback hold two each. Open license, Modularity, Metadata, and Editable source hold one each. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one fix and the eight metric bins. 2. The learner may open the fix summary table. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner places the fix in a bin, and the placement is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After fix 13 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 13 fixes in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [metric]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This fix mainly raises [metric]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 13 correct on the first attempt". At 11 or more it adds "You can pick the fix for a low metric." Below 11 it lists the Why text of each missed fix. **Starting State:** The first fix in the shuffled order and the eight bins. The question shown is "Which metric does this fix mainly raise?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of thirteen fixes names the same metric for each fix.
